definitions: To exaggerate the importance or difficulty of a minor problem.
To treat a trivial matter as if it were a serious crisis.
examples: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill; it's just a small scratch.
She tends to make a mountain out of a molehill when things don't go her way.
It's not worth making a mountain out of a molehill over a spilled drink.
lemma: to make a mountain out of a molehill
source: to make a mountain out of a molehill
